Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace as a canonical object
Decision_Register.decision: M04 is the sole canonical owner of MarketplaceContext, including marketplace identity, tenant and owner references, participating organizations, channels, brand, product presentation, routing, attribution, support identity, disclosures, domains, lifecycle, readiness, effective dates and version history. Other modules may retain the marketplace identifier and version used by a transaction but may not create competing marketplace records.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: One marketplace per tenant
Decision_Register.decision: Each Lucie tenant has exactly one canonical marketplace and no more than one active production marketplace. Consumer-direct, agent, employer, product, carrier, state and direct-downline variations are represented as governed configuration or context within that marketplace rather than separate marketplaces.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace owner
Decision_Register.decision: Every marketplace has exactly one owning organization. The owner is the M05 tenant-owning root agency for a customer tenant and the JET organization for the JET internal tenant. A direct downline may participate but cannot own an independent marketplace. Ownership changes only through a governed tenant-ownership transition.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Initial marketplace creation
Decision_Register.decision: When M05 creates a tenant and root organization, M04 creates one linked DRAFT marketplace with immutable marketplace ID, tenant and owner references, internal code, working display name, English default, eligible M00 channel references, baseline or empty brand, readiness checklist and no public production route. The root completes routine setup; JET only repairs or replaces through an explicit platform operation.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace administration authority
Decision_Register.decision: An authorized root AGENCY_ADMIN may configure identity, brand, support, enabled entitled channels and product lines, routing choices, participant attribution, approved disclosures, domain request, preview, readiness, initial-activation submission, business suspension or reactivation, and history. JET may perform all actions and retains initial production activation, legal and security blocks, domain routing, emergency suspension, final override, owner-transition control and platform reference stewardship. No separate Marketplace Operator role is introduced.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Downline administration posture
Decision_Register.decision: A direct downline may view its marketplace participation, enabled channels and product lines, readiness, responsible support and attribution, and may maintain permitted M05 support information or request correction. It cannot change global brand, domain, product visibility, tenant routing, legal disclosures, other participants, provider routes or marketplace lifecycle. Root authority prevails.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace participant model
Decision_Register.decision: The root is always the primary participant. Each active direct downline is an eligible participant that the root explicitly enables. Participation states are NOT_ENABLED, PENDING_READINESS, ENABLED and SUSPENDED. Participation may enable attribution, assignment, assistance and routed work but creates no separate marketplace, storefront, entitlement, provider route, selling authority or affiliation.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Relationship and participation changes
Decision_Register.decision: M04 reevaluates participation when M05 creates, activates, suspends, ends or changes a relevant organization or relationship. New downlines are not automatically enabled. Relationship end or downline suspension stops new attribution and routing, preserves historical responsibility, requires explicit open-work treatment and never silently moves submitted or final records.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Supported channels
Decision_Register.decision: One marketplace may support any approved subset of CONSUMER_DIRECT, AGENT and EMPLOYER. Separate marketplaces are not created by channel. IFP, dental and vision may use consumer-direct and agent where their pathways are ready; ICHRA employer quoting may use employer and agent. Root administrators may enable only channels commercially entitled and activated by M00.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace lifecycle
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace lifecycle is fixed to DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED and ENDED. Draft supports configuration and preview only; Active permits production only when every applicable dependency and gate passes; Suspended prevents new public journeys; Ended permanently closes new activity and preserves history. Readiness and review remain workflow states, not lifecycle values.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace readiness
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace readiness is derived separately from lifecycle and evaluates active tenant and owner, valid MarketplaceContext, complete English and Spanish brand content, valid assets and domain, support identity, at least one enabled entitled channel and ready product pathway, product visibility, attribution, routing, disclosure assignment, dependency health and absence of a JET block. Users cannot manually mark failed controls as passed.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Initial production activation
Decision_Register.decision: The root submits the completed draft marketplace for initial production activation. JET activates only after confirming readiness, commercial entitlement, route, bilingual and legal content, product and geography readiness, support ownership, security, accessibility, UAT and required M00, M05 and M01 delta disposition. The decision and evidence are recorded; initial activation is never automatic or root-only.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Business suspension and reactivation
Decision_Register.decision: After initial activation, a root administrator may suspend the marketplace with a fixed reason, effective date, user-safe unavailable message, active-journey review, confirmation and audit, and may reactivate when readiness passes and no JET block exists. JET may suspend or reactivate for security, legal, contractual, platform or operational reasons and takes precedence. M00 emergency controls may disable individual capabilities without suspending the whole marketplace.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Suspended-marketplace consumer continuity
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace suspension blocks new anonymous entry and new quote, product, employer and marketplace-based agent starts but does not automatically remove safe access to existing saved quotes, applications, enrollment records, documents, required next actions and support for authenticated users. The suspended storefront presents a controlled message and permitted sign-in or record route. Tenant, account, legal or emergency controls may still block access.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace ending
Decision_Register.decision: A root may request ending, but only JET may complete it as part of offboarding or approved transition. Ending requires disposition of open journeys, saved quotes, applications, handoffs, member access, documents, communications, participants, domains, redirects, support, exports, retention, audit and M01 continuity. An ended marketplace accepts no new activity, cannot be routinely reactivated and never deletes transaction or audit history.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace replacement and rebranding
Decision_Register.decision: Brand, support, product presentation and domain changes create effective-dated versions of the same marketplace. A new marketplace is not created for a name, logo, color, support, domain, channel or product-line change. A successor marketplace is considered only for a new tenant, legally distinct owner transition, governed migration or future approved marketplace model. Cloning and parallel production storefronts are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace context persistence
Decision_Register.decision: The marketplace resolved at journey entry remains attached through anonymous browsing, authentication, household, quote, PlanAI, cart, assistance, application, signature, handoff, documents, communications, enrollment and Member Workspace. Marketplace and relevant release versions are preserved for reconstruction. Later changes do not rewrite the context used by completed transactions.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Global consumer identity across marketplaces
Decision_Register.decision: Consumers use one global M00 identity across marketplaces. Entering another storefront changes context only for a new journey and does not merge or move households, quotes, applications, documents, agent relationships or enrollments. The active marketplace brand and responsible agency remain visible. Cross-marketplace transfer requires explicit authorized share, reassignment or handoff.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: JET marketplace parity
Decision_Register.decision: The JET marketplace uses the same MarketplaceContext, lifecycle, readiness, brand, routing, attribution, disclosure and audit contracts as customer marketplaces. JET is both owner and platform administrator. Differences arise from governed configuration and ownership, not a hardcoded separate application.

Decision_Register.topic: Marketplace Establishment, Ownership and Lifecycle
Decision_Register.title: Future marketplace boundary
Decision_Register.decision: Contracts preserve stable identifiers, ownership, versioning and adapters for future multiple marketplaces per tenant, downline storefronts, employer microsites, carrier-operated marketplaces, marketplace networks, concurrent domains, richer themes, marketplace-specific provider routes and more complex participants. Lucie does not build their screens, routing or operations in this release.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: White-label scope
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie provides limited controlled white labeling, not a website builder. Root administrators may configure display name, logo, primary and accent colors, optional hero image, headline, short introduction, consumer support identity, public domain and approved footer or attribution. Information architecture, layouts, components, workflows, forms, validation, accessibility and transaction content remain fixed; custom CSS, JavaScript, navigation, pages, forms and agency-authored workflow behavior are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: One active marketplace brand
Decision_Register.decision: Each marketplace has one active brand configuration shared across consumer-direct, agent-assisted, employer, account, Member Workspace, unavailable and error surfaces. Separate kits by channel, product, carrier, state, downline, role or segment are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Brand administration authority
Decision_Register.decision: Authorized root administrators configure routine brand changes. Downlines may view the brand and maintain permitted M05 support data only. JET may view, edit, block, revert, replace invalid assets, enforce legal or security restrictions, disable a presentation element or restore the JET baseline. JET is not responsible for routine agency branding.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Brand asset inventory
Decision_Register.decision: The MVP asset inventory is one primary logo, one compact or square logo, one favicon and one optional hero image. The platform produces required variants. Per-page galleries, video, animation, campaigns, media libraries, downline assets and carrier themes are excluded. Missing optional assets use an approved baseline, never broken placeholders.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Color customization
Decision_Register.decision: The root chooses one primary and one accent color. Lucie derives accessible shades, text, hover, focus and component variants. Success, warning, error, security and status colors remain platform-controlled. Inaccessible combinations cannot be published. No full design-token editor is exposed.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Typography
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie uses one JET-approved accessible font family. Agencies cannot upload or select fonts. Brand differentiation comes from logo, approved colors, imagery and marketplace identity, avoiding licensing, layout, accessibility and bilingual-rendering risk.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Fixed layouts and components
Decision_Register.decision: All marketplaces use the fixed Lucie layout and component system. Root administrators may populate approved fields and choose limited presentation options but cannot rearrange header or footer, move disclosures, remove support or language controls, alter navigation, hide accessibility controls or replace platform forms. Michael designs one reusable system, not bespoke customer interfaces.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace display identity
Decision_Register.decision: A marketplace may have a consumer-facing display name and tagline plus owning-root display and legal names where required. The marketplace name may differ from legal name, but legal ownership remains available in legal or footer areas. Misleading claims of carrier, government, Exchange or regulated status are prohibited and may be blocked by JET.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Home-page content
Decision_Register.decision: The fixed marketplace home includes logo and name, optional hero image, headline, short description, enabled pathway cards, language picker, support, required legal and platform attribution and returning-user sign-in. The root may customize headline and introduction in both languages; workflow buttons, eligibility language, regulated instructions and transaction labels remain system-controlled. No unrestricted marketing-page builder is included.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Channel presentation
Decision_Register.decision: Enabled consumer-direct, agent and employer pathways appear through fixed Lucie cards and landing experiences. Root administrators may enable entitled channels, provide short approved bilingual introductions and choose approved imagery or baseline presentation. They cannot redesign flows or create channel types.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Downline presentation
Decision_Register.decision: Direct downlines operate under the root marketplace brand and may be shown contextually through responsible agency, assigned agent, support and approved relationship disclosure. They receive no separate theme, hero, domain, logo, navigation or product-presentation system.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: ABox and JET attribution
Decision_Register.decision: The root agency is the primary brand. ABox or JET attribution may appear in restrained footer, legal, secure sign-in, support or handoff contexts when contractually, legally or operationally required. JET centrally controls mandatory, optional or hidden treatment; roots cannot remove required attribution.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: English and Spanish content
Decision_Register.decision: Every activated marketplace has complete English and Spanish presentation. Each root-configurable text field requires both languages; custom agency content is not machine translated. Incomplete Spanish cannot route users into English-only experience. An approved bilingual JET baseline is used when custom copy is absent.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Language selection
Decision_Register.decision: English is default and a persistent English or Espanol picker applies across browsing, sign-in, shopping, PlanAI, assistance, application, handoff, account and Member Workspace. After authentication, the M00 profile preference is authoritative. Language changes do not restart or change marketplace, responsible agency or saved data.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: General marketplace copy
Decision_Register.decision: Root administrators may edit limited non-regulated plain text or safe-format fields: headline, introduction, channel introductions, support introduction and agency description, subject to length and content rules. Scripts, embedded apps, unsupported HTML, tracking pixels, pricing or eligibility claims and unapproved affiliation claims are prohibited. JET may block misleading or unsafe content.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Legal and regulated content
Decision_Register.decision: JET controls legal, privacy, consent, eligibility, enrollment, PlanAI and regulated content through an approved bilingual library. Roots may select applicable approved items or variants and supply required references but may not rewrite controlled text. Accepted disclosures retain the exact content version and language presented.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Content and brand versions
Decision_Register.decision: Brand and content versions use DRAFT, ACTIVE and SUPERSEDED. One active and one editable draft are allowed, with unlimited historical superseded versions. Draft preview does not affect production. Publishing creates a new active version and preserves history for audit and transaction reconstruction.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Brand publishing authority
Decision_Register.decision: JET performs initial marketplace activation. After launch, roots may self-publish ordinary low-risk brand and general-copy changes when both languages, assets, accessibility, legal-content integrity and readiness pass and no JET block exists. JET approval remains required for initial activation, custom-domain activation, ownership change, material regulated content, reviewed changes and restoration after JET suspension. No configurable approval workflow is added.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Scheduled brand changes
Decision_Register.decision: A root may publish immediately or schedule one future effective date and time. Repeating schedules, audience targeting, percentage rollout, A/B tests, seasonal campaign calendars and multiple queued brand versions are excluded. JET may cancel or delay a blocked schedule.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace preview
Decision_Register.decision: Private preview supports English and Spanish, consumer, agent and employer entry, desktop, tablet and mobile, draft assets and content, support, disclosures, unavailable, suspended and error states. Preview is visibly nonproduction, not indexed and cannot create quotes, applications, messages, signatures or handoffs.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Public domain options
Decision_Register.decision: Each marketplace may use a default JET-managed subdomain or an agency-owned custom domain. An agency may move to a custom domain without a new marketplace. Exactly one domain is the primary public production entry.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Custom-domain administration
Decision_Register.decision: The root may request a custom domain and is responsible for ownership, external verification, registration maintenance and non-misleading use. JET verifies and activates the route, applies platform security, blocks invalid domains and handles emergencies. Agencies never receive direct routing, certificate, infrastructure or secret administration.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: One primary production domain
Decision_Register.decision: A marketplace has exactly one active primary production domain. A controlled JET service route, temporary redirect from the previous domain and nonproduction preview routes may coexist without becoming additional marketplaces. Multiple public domains cannot create conflicting identity or tracking contexts.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Domain change and continuity
Decision_Register.decision: A domain change creates a new effective route version. JET may redirect a prior controlled route during transition. Existing journeys retain canonical MarketplaceContext and are not duplicated. Sign-in, secure links where valid, record access, audit, bilingual communication and support continuity are preserved.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Invalid or unavailable domain behavior
Decision_Register.decision: Unknown, unverified, expired, suspended or incorrectly mapped domains fail closed and never route silently to another agency, JET marketplace, tenant or generic shopping. A controlled unavailable message and approved support route may be shown. Any JET service route must be explicitly configured and identify the correct marketplace.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Search-engine presentation
Decision_Register.decision: M04 supports only basic bilingual page title and description, marketplace name, primary domain and approved preview image. Draft, preview and suspended routes are not indexed. Active indexing requires JET enablement. SEO consoles, campaigns, structured-data editing, blogs, landing-page farms and agency tracking scripts are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Brand application across Lucie
Decision_Register.decision: The active brand applies wherever a MarketplaceContext exists: public entry, shopping, authentication presentation, consumer and member workspaces, employer, unavailable and error states, secure links, communications and generated outputs where consuming modules support it. M04 supplies brand and version; M00, M10, M13 and others apply it. SMS uses sender and responsible-agency identity rather than visual styling.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Historical brand preservation
Decision_Register.decision: Material transactions retain the marketplace and brand-content version used at the time. Historical documents and communications are not regenerated after logo, color, name, domain, support or copy changes. Current account surfaces may show current support while historical evidence remains unchanged and dated.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Brand and content enforcement
Decision_Register.decision: M04 validates every proposed brand and content version. Missing bilingual content, invalid assets, inaccessible colors, prohibited or misleading content, missing support or disclosures, invalid domain and JET legal, security or contractual block prevent publication. JET may suspend or revert serious issues while exposing reason, corrective action and prior valid version to the root.

Decision_Register.topic: Storefront Branding, Domains and Bilingual Content
Decision_Register.title: Future white-label boundary
Decision_Register.decision: Contracts preserve future seams for multiple brand kits, downline storefronts, employer microsites, carrier brands, custom fonts, richer themes, content pages, campaigns, banners, multiple domains, A/B testing, custom analytics and marketplace-specific communication templates. The MVP implements none of those simply because it is called white labeling.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace availability decision
Decision_Register.decision: A marketplace product pathway is presented only when tenant, marketplace, M00 commercial activation, product-line entitlement, channel entitlement, marketplace channel and product visibility, launch geography, M03 product and plan readiness, carrier pathway readiness, participant readiness, M08 authority, provider and integration readiness, feature controls, launch gates and absence of a JET block all pass. M04 composes the final presentation decision but does not duplicate any source module calculation.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Fixed Lucie product-line catalogue
Decision_Register.decision: The fixed Lucie product-line catalogue is IFP_ON_EXCHANGE, IFP_OFF_EXCHANGE, DENTAL, VISION and ICHRA_EMPLOYER_QUOTING. Root agencies cannot create, rename or reclassify canonical product lines. Future ancillary or custom products require governed downstream expansion.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Product-visibility granularity
Decision_Register.decision: Root administrators configure marketplace visibility only at State, Product line and Carrier levels. They do not curate plan by plan. When a carrier is enabled for a state and product line, every M03-published plan that passes channel, geography, effective-date, legal and readiness controls is eligible. JET may block an individual product or plan for a governed issue.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Carrier selection
Decision_Register.decision: Root administrators select only JET-controlled carrier organizations with ready product data for the applicable state and product line. Carrier presentation does not create appointments, contracts, integrations, commissions or selling authority and cannot override M08 or downstream readiness.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: State product-line and carrier matrix
Decision_Register.decision: M04 exposes one simple State to Product line to Carrier availability matrix. A root may enable an approved state, an entitled product line and ready carriers. The UI explains blockers. Arbitrary Boolean rules, county-authored rules, consumer-segment or household rules, date formulas, custom eligibility expressions and scripting are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Geography model
Decision_Register.decision: One marketplace may serve multiple JET-approved launch states. The root selects only approved states for its tenant. Separate state marketplaces, brands, domains, root-authored counties, service areas or geography definitions are excluded. M03 service-area data controls exact plan geography.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Consumer service-area resolution
Decision_Register.decision: Before exact products are shown, the user provides the minimum location data required by the pathway. Approved geography and M03 service-area data resolve state, county or rating area, service area, carriers and plans. Roots cannot force plans outside their published service area. Unresolvable location enters a clear correction flow rather than estimated availability.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Supported channel and product combinations
Decision_Register.decision: Supported combinations are fixed: on-exchange IFP supports consumer-direct and agent; off-exchange IFP supports consumer-direct and agent when ready; dental and vision support consumer-direct and agent when M21 and dependent pathways are ready; ICHRA employer quoting supports employer and agent and is not consumer-direct in the initial Lucie scope. New combinations require governed change.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace channel control
Decision_Register.decision: The root may enable or disable commercially entitled CONSUMER_DIRECT, AGENT and EMPLOYER channels. Disabling removes new public entry but preserves existing journeys and evidence. JET may disable a channel for legal, product, integration, security, contractual or release reasons. A root cannot enable an unentitled or inactive channel.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Product-line control
Decision_Register.decision: The root may enable or disable an entitled product line within each enabled state. Disablement is prospective: it stops new entries and removes public presentation while preserving quotes, applications, documents, handoffs, enrollment and coverage. Reenablement requires current readiness.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Carrier disablement
Decision_Register.decision: The root may stop presenting a carrier for new activity by state and product line. Existing quotes, submitted applications, coverage, documents, external results and historical attribution remain unchanged. JET may immediately disable a carrier or product for compliance, data or operational risk.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: No marketplace-controlled plan ranking
Decision_Register.decision: M04 does not permit manual plan ranking, sponsorship, promotion or individual-plan suppression by a root agency. Ordering, comparison and recommendation remain with M01, M02 and PlanAI. Carrier visibility cannot imply recommendation. Paid placement and offer ranking remain future downstream boundaries.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Product availability version
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace availability configuration is versioned independently using DRAFT, ACTIVE and SUPERSEDED. There is one active version, one editable draft and historical superseded versions. Publishing creates a new active version and preserves the configuration used by earlier journeys and transactions.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Effective-date scheduling
Decision_Register.decision: A root may publish an approved availability version immediately or at one future effective date and time. Recurring schedules, multiple queued versions, percentage rollouts, audience or household targeting and date formulas are excluded. JET may delay or cancel a blocked activation.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Public product presentation before quoting
Decision_Register.decision: The public marketplace may show high-level categories before account creation, but it cannot promise a specific carrier or plan before required location and shopping information is collected. Exact plans, prices, subsidies, benefits and eligibility are displayed only through the governed shopping or quoting pathway.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Hidden versus unavailable presentation
Decision_Register.decision: Ordinary users see only enabled channels and product lines. A deep link to an unavailable pathway shows a controlled, marketplace-branded unavailable state with an approved next action and no internal configuration detail. Root and JET administrators see potential pathways and their entitlement, product, geography, carrier, participant, integration and launch blockers.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: No generic coming-soon catalogue
Decision_Register.decision: Unavailable products, states, carriers and channels are not shown as coming soon by default. JET may approve an accurate bilingual informational message that avoids unsupported dates, distinguishes interest from active shopping and does not collect application data. M04 is not a wait-list or launch-marketing platform.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: No silent fallback
Decision_Register.decision: M04 never silently changes marketplace, marketplace context, exchange posture, channel, responsible agency, carrier or real-versus-estimated availability when a requested pathway is unavailable. Any alternative requires explicit user choice.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Alternative-channel offer
Decision_Register.decision: When self-service is unavailable but an approved agent-assisted path exists in the same marketplace, Lucie may explicitly offer assistance, scheduling, an available or assigned agent and permitted data preservation. The experience explains the channel change, assisting agency, data access, authorization and any re-entry requirement before the user accepts.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Switching between consumer-direct and agent assistance
Decision_Register.decision: A consumer may explicitly move from self-service to agent assistance within the same marketplace. Where permitted, marketplace, identity, household, geography, product line, quote inputs and quote or cart reference are preserved. Actual actor, consumer authorization, responsible organization, assigned agent and marketplace and availability versions remain historical. M01, M02 and M09 own detailed assistance and assignment behavior.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: On-exchange IFP entry
Decision_Register.decision: When on-exchange IFP is enabled, M04 enters the protected M01 journey with marketplace and release, tenant, responsible organization, channel, state, language, attribution, support and product-line context. M01 remains authoritative for quote, comparison, PlanAI, cart, consent and JET EDE handoff; M04 does not duplicate shopping.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: On-exchange and off-exchange choice
Decision_Register.decision: When both on-exchange and off-exchange IFP are active, Lucie presents a fixed plain-language choice distinguishing Marketplace shopping that may include financial assistance from direct purchase without Marketplace financial assistance. M04 does not promise subsidy eligibility, determine legal eligibility, automatically select a path or hide material differences.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Off-exchange IFP pathway
Decision_Register.decision: Off-exchange IFP may be configured in M04 but remains hidden from production until M02, M26, carrier, document, signature and integration dependencies are ready. Once active, it uses the same marketplace brand, language, support and attribution contracts. No temporary substitute application or simulated production outcome is allowed.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Dental and vision pathways
Decision_Register.decision: Dental and vision visibility may be configured but remains unavailable until M21, M02, M26 and carrier pathways are ready. M04 controls category, state, carrier and channel presentation; M21 and shopping and enrollment owners determine standalone, bundled, add-on and application behavior. M04 does not invent bundling.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: ICHRA employer pathway
Decision_Register.decision: When ICHRA employer quoting is enabled, M04 presents employer and agent entry into M20 and supplies marketplace, tenant, responsible organization, channel, language, support, geography and release context. M20 owns employer identity, quote, employee or class structure, contributions, workflow and final availability. ICHRA is not consumer-direct in initial Lucie.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Participant readiness and product availability
Decision_Register.decision: An agent-assisted pathway is available only when at least one appropriate organization and workforce participant can support the product, carrier, geography and channel. M04 consumes M05 participation, M06 affiliation and readiness and M08 authority but does not calculate sellability. If no eligible seller exists, the pathway is blocked or sent to approved root support rather than falsely shown as available.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Consumer-direct participant posture
Decision_Register.decision: A consumer-direct journey does not require agent selection when the pathway supports unassisted activity. The marketplace still records owner, responsible organization, support identity and attribution. If a legal, carrier or pathway rule requires a producer, the path remains unavailable until a valid assignment exists.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: No-ready-products behavior
Decision_Register.decision: When no ready products exist for the selected geography, product line, channel and marketplace, Lucie presents a clear no-options result and may offer location correction, another enabled category, assistance, support or return-later. It never displays stale, cross-state, cross-marketplace or simulated plans. Administration exposes the actual canonical blocker.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Product-pathway preview
Decision_Register.decision: Root and JET administrators may preview product and channel availability using approved state, product, channel, participant, language and ready or blocked conditions. Preview uses read-only or test data, is clearly nonproduction and cannot create consumers, quotes, applications, messages, assignments or handoffs.

Decision_Register.topic: Product, Channel and Shopping-Path Availability
Decision_Register.title: Historical availability preservation
Decision_Register.decision: Every material journey and transaction retains the marketplace availability version used at start or relevant selection. Later changes do not silently alter quote contents, product line, carrier, channel, responsible organization, application, signature, handoff or enrollment. Resuming an old unfinished journey clearly identifies if refresh or restart is required by the owning module.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace participant types
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace participants are the tenant-owning root agency, root-enabled direct downline agencies and workforce users or agents associated through M06. Organizations are canonical participants; agents and staff participate through M00 identity, M06 affiliation and M08 authority. M04 creates no marketplace-specific agency identity, agent profile, storefront entity, custom participant type or relationship graph.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Root-agency participation
Decision_Register.decision: The root agency is always the primary participant, marketplace owner, primary brand, default support organization, recipient of unassigned work, overseer of direct downlines and continuity provider when a participant is unavailable. It cannot remove itself while it owns the tenant.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Direct-downline eligibility
Decision_Register.decision: A direct downline is eligible only when its M05 organization and PARENT_OF relationship are active, the root enables participation, an active administrator exists, required M06 profile and support readiness passes, applicable channel and product readiness passes and no M00, M05, M08, legal or JET block exists. Eligibility is reevaluated whenever a dependency changes.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Participant configuration
Decision_Register.decision: Each eligible downline has a fixed participant record with participation state, effective dates, consumer-assistance, agent and employer channel participation, responsible-agency display preference, support-identity preference, referral-link availability and current readiness. Custom fields, participant-authored routing or participant-specific product catalogues are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Agent participation boundary
Decision_Register.decision: An agent may participate only with an active M00 account, active M06 affiliation and workforce profile, applicable M08 license, appointment, credential and sellability, required assignment or assistance basis and no suspension or JET block. M04 consumes the eligible-agent result and never calculates authority.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace attribution roles
Decision_Register.decision: M04 distinguishes marketplace owner, entry-attribution organization, current responsible organization, assigned agent, selling organization and producer, and current support organization. These roles may coincide but are never assumed equivalent. Historical records preserve each role and the governing source.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Default consumer-direct responsibility
Decision_Register.decision: A new consumer-direct journey through the normal public domain defaults to the root as responsible organization and remains self-service unless a producer is required. The root may retain, assign assistance, reassign eligible open work to a downline or respond to assistance requests. Normal public entries are not automatically distributed among downlines.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Downline referral links
Decision_Register.decision: An enabled downline may have one system-generated referral link on the shared marketplace domain and brand. It identifies the downline as entry-attribution and initial responsible organization for a new journey while preserving owner and marketplace. It creates no storefront, domain, record access or selling authority and may be revoked by the downline, root or JET.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Agent referral links
Decision_Register.decision: An eligible agent may have one system-generated referral link tied to marketplace, responsible agency, agent, approved channel and optional approved product-line entry. It may establish intended responsibility and assignment for a new journey if eligibility remains valid. It does not grant existing-record access, bypass consent or sellability, guarantee assignment, create an agent storefront or determine commissions.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Referral-link administration
Decision_Register.decision: The root may create, view, revoke and replace referral links for root, direct downlines and eligible agents, review status and basic usage, and disable participant links. A downline may manage its own agency and affiliated-agent links. An agent may copy and use an active link but cannot change its organization or marketplace. JET may disable or replace any link.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Referral links are not security credentials
Decision_Register.decision: A referral link establishes entry attribution only and is never a credential. Returning consumers must authenticate for protected records, existing responsibility and consent remain controlling, and the referred agency or agent receives no automatic record access. Existing-record access requires a new approved authorization or assignment basis where applicable.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Invalid or unavailable referral link
Decision_Register.decision: If a referral link references an unavailable agent or organization, Lucie never silently substitutes another participant. It offers explicit choices such as same agency without named agent, root marketplace, root assistance, home page or support based on readiness. The user's selection determines new responsibility. Marketplace unavailability uses the normal unavailable treatment.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Existing journey takes precedence
Decision_Register.decision: An existing saved or active journey retains its marketplace, responsible organization, assigned agent, channel, product line and availability version. A later referral link never silently moves it. The consumer may resume, explicitly start a separate journey in the new context or request a governed transfer or assistance change.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Signed-in new-journey confirmation
Decision_Register.decision: A signed-in consumer starting a new journey through a different referral context sees and confirms the marketplace, proposed responsible agency and agent, product line, channel, new-journey status and the fact that existing records will not move before the new journey is created.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: No public agency or agent directory
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie provides no public agency or agent directory, ratings, specialties, office browsing or availability calendar. A participant is reached through normal marketplace entry, approved referral link, existing assignment, consumer-requested assistance or root-authorized reassignment.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Fixed routing sequence
Decision_Register.decision: New-journey routing follows this fixed order: preserve an existing active journey; valid agent referral; valid downline referral; existing authorized relationship confirmed by the owning module; otherwise normal marketplace entry to the root. A later signal never silently overrides an earlier valid governing condition.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: No automatic round-robin in the MVP
Decision_Register.decision: Lucie does not implement round-robin, weighted, capacity, geographic-radius, performance, language, specialty, commission, AI scoring, calendar or conversion-based routing. Unassigned work enters the responsible organization's fixed logical queue and is assigned through M09, M06 or the owning journey workflow.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Consumer assistance request
Decision_Register.decision: A consumer may explicitly request assistance from an eligible self-service journey. Where permitted, the request preserves marketplace, responsibility, identity, household, geography, product, quote inputs, record reference, language and attribution. The user is told which agency receives it, whether an agent exists, which data becomes visible, the required authorization and next step. M01, M02 and M09 own detailed work.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Responsible-organization queue
Decision_Register.decision: Each root or enabled downline participant has one logical marketplace queue for assistance requests, unassigned referrals, employer assistance, routing exceptions, unavailable-agent items and reassignment requests. M04 identifies responsible organization and routing reason; M00 owns shared tasks and exceptions; business modules own the work record. Custom marketplace queues are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Root assignment authority
Decision_Register.decision: A root administrator may assign or reassign eligible open marketplace work among the root, direct enabled downlines and eligible agents within the selected responsible organization. Current and proposed responsibility, agent, reason, effective time, required notice, consent review and audit are mandatory. Submitted, signed, handed-off or final records cannot use ordinary reassignment.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Downline assignment authority
Decision_Register.decision: A downline administrator may assign or reassign eligible work among eligible agents affiliated with its own organization only. It cannot assign siblings, move work to or from root without root authority, select another agency's agent, override sellability, move final evidence or change marketplace ownership. Root authority may override.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Agent readiness loss
Decision_Register.decision: When an assigned or referred agent loses account, affiliation, credential, appointment, sellability or organization readiness, new routing and the referral link stop immediately, open work is flagged, responsibility stays with the organization until governed reassignment, self-service may continue when permitted and producer-required work remains blocked. Historical attribution remains.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Named agent unavailable experience
Decision_Register.decision: When a named agent is unavailable, the marketplace explicitly offers same agency without named agent, another eligible agent from that agency, root assistance, self-service where permitted or return home. Another agent is never silently substituted.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Employer-pathway routing
Decision_Register.decision: A new employer journey through normal entry defaults to the root. A valid downline or agent referral may establish initial responsibility or assignment when enabled for EMPLOYER. M04 supplies context; M20 owns employer matching, contact authority, quote ownership, assignment and ICHRA workflow. Existing employer work is not changed by a later referral.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Consumer-facing agency presentation
Decision_Register.decision: Consumer-facing experiences clearly distinguish marketplace brand, marketplace owner, current responsible agency, assigned agent where applicable and support contact on relevant journey, assistance, quote, application, communication, account, member and handoff surfaces without implying a downline owns a separate marketplace.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Support-identity hierarchy
Decision_Register.decision: Every marketplace has a complete bilingual root support identity with display name, phone, secure email or contact route, business hours, support introduction and escalation reference where applicable. An enabled downline may use contextual support sourced from M05 while retaining root marketplace brand and owner attribution. Root may override or replace downline presentation.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Support fallback
Decision_Register.decision: Root support is the fixed fallback when no downline is responsible, downline support is incomplete, the downline or relationship is inactive, no active administrator exists or a routing or support exception remains. Stale downline support is never shown. Current root support may be displayed without rewriting historical responsibility.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Support ownership by issue type
Decision_Register.decision: Support ownership is lean: responsible agency handles ordinary shopping, quote, assistance and application questions; root handles downline escalation, unassigned work, continuity and marketplace administration; JET handles platform, identity, security, integration and unresolved product defects; authoritative external outcomes route to the relevant carrier, Exchange, employer or provider. Users see one primary route.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Communications and document attribution
Decision_Register.decision: M04 supplies M10, M13 and transaction modules with marketplace and brand version, owner, entry attribution, responsible organization, assigned agent, support identity, language and routing version. Communications and outputs use the approved transaction context. Later assignment or support changes do not rewrite sent communications, signed documents or completed evidence.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Consent and agent record access
Decision_Register.decision: Entry through an agency or agent referral link does not authorize access to existing consumer records. New journeys may establish responsibility and intended assignment, while existing records require consumer assistance authorization, assignment, takeover, sharing permission or another approved basis preserving purpose, scope, actor, organization, language, version and time.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Attribution and assignment history
Decision_Register.decision: Each marketplace journey retains append-only history of entry source, marketplace, entry-attribution organization, initial and current responsible organization, agent history, selling organization and producer where applicable, support organization, routing and reassignment reason, effective dates, actual actor, consumer authorization and marketplace and routing versions. Reassignment is prospective.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Fixed entry-source catalogue
Decision_Register.decision: Entry source is fixed to MARKETPLACE_DIRECT, ROOT_AGENCY_LINK, DOWNLINE_AGENCY_LINK, AGENT_LINK, ROOT_ADMIN_INITIATED, DOWNLINE_ADMIN_INITIATED, EMPLOYER_LINK, EXISTING_AUTHORIZED_RELATIONSHIP and APPROVED_EXTERNAL_REFERRAL. Standard analytics parameters may be retained but never independently control routing or authorization. No custom source builder is included.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Participant suspension and ending
Decision_Register.decision: Participant suspension or ending stops new routing, attribution, referral links and agent assignments, flags open work for continuity and permits root reassignment of eligible work while preserving completed history and providing updated support. It does not end or delete the M05 organization and cannot reactivate against inactive M05 state.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Routing explanation for administrators
Decision_Register.decision: Root and JET administrators can inspect routing explanation showing entry source, referral link, existing relationship where used, selected organization and agent, eligibility checks, fallback or user choice, routing version and time. Downline administrators see only their records. Consumers receive a simpler who-is-helping and change-request explanation.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: No commission or contract determination
Decision_Register.decision: M04 attribution, responsibility and routing do not determine commission ownership, revenue sharing, writing hierarchy, book ownership, carrier contract, selling paper, appointment, producer of record or policy-servicing ownership. M04 preserves factual marketplace history for M06, M07, M08, M12, M18 and transaction modules.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Future routing boundary
Decision_Register.decision: Contracts preserve future seams for round-robin, weighted, capacity, skill and language matching, proximity, availability calendars, public agent directories, AI lead routing, performance routing, call-center queues, multiple responsible organizations and cross-tenant referrals. None are implemented in Lucie MVP.

Decision_Register.topic: Participants, Attribution, Routing and Support Identity
Decision_Register.title: Complete prior-module continuity
Decision_Register.decision: M04 produces complete impact and proposed append-only delta records for every affected M00, M05 and protected M01 requirement, role, context, screen, API, event, integration, consent, notification, audit, export, migration and regression obligation. No delivered baseline is silently changed.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Fixed marketplace-administration surfaces
Decision_Register.decision: M04 provides fixed Marketplace Administration Home, Identity and Brand, Content and Language, Domains and Public Routes, Channels and Availability, Participants and Referral Links, Routing and Support, Readiness, Preview and Publication, and History and Operational Issues surfaces. JET, root and downline actions vary by authority. Custom pages, navigation, dashboards and user-created marketplace sections are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace Administration Home
Decision_Register.decision: The root Marketplace Administration Home shows lifecycle, domain, active release, draft and scheduled change, channels, states, product lines, carriers, participants, links, readiness, product and participant problems, recent changes, open work and quick actions for preview, edit, publish, suspend and history. It is an operational summary, not a configurable analytics dashboard.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Guided initial marketplace setup
Decision_Register.decision: Initial setup follows a fixed guided sequence: identity; assets and colors; English and Spanish content; root support; channels; state, product and carrier availability; downline participation; routing and referral posture; JET subdomain or custom domain; preview; readiness; and submission for initial JET activation. Draft save and resume is supported. No configurable onboarding workflow is included.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Draft save and resume
Decision_Register.decision: Marketplace administration automatically preserves draft progress and distinguishes saved draft, unsaved local change, validation problem, readiness blocker, scheduled publication and active production configuration. Only one editable draft exists for each governed configuration stream; competing administrator-owned drafts are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace administration authority
Decision_Register.decision: Every authorized root AGENCY_ADMIN has the same governed marketplace administration authority. No separate Marketplace Administrator, brand-only or product-only role, per-field permission model or agency-defined approval hierarchy is introduced. M00 may distinguish high-risk operations; downline authority remains limited to approved view and correction requests.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Coordinated marketplace-release snapshot
Decision_Register.decision: Brand, availability, routing, participant, support, domain and disclosure records retain their own histories but are published through one coordinated MarketplaceRelease that references their exact versions. There is one active release, one editable draft release and historical superseded releases. Each journey retains the release version used.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Active-versus-draft comparison
Decision_Register.decision: Before publication, root and JET administrators compare active and draft values, effective date, affected channels, states, products, carriers, participants, public presentation, support and blockers. The comparison explains business effect, such as which new journeys stop, rather than only raw field differences.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace preview modes
Decision_Register.decision: Private preview supports language, device, consumer, agent or employer entry, state, product line, root or downline attribution, normal or referral entry and ready, blocked, suspended or unavailable state. Selected conditions are visible. Preview is nonproduction and creates no business record.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Participant-context preview
Decision_Register.decision: The root may preview normal root entry, selected downline entry, eligible agent referral, named-agent-unavailable and suspended-participant states. Preview shows brand, owner, entry attribution, responsible organization, agent, support and required disclosure without granting or impersonating participant access.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Publication review and confirmation
Decision_Register.decision: Before publishing or scheduling, Lucie presents marketplace and tenant, effective time, brand, domain, channel, product, state, carrier, participant, routing, support, legal or disclosure, continuity, blocker, warning and required-approval changes. The administrator confirms the coordinated release; incomplete sections are never published separately.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Initial activation submission
Decision_Register.decision: The root submits initial setup to JET. It may correct an unapproved draft, but material changes after review starts return affected items to pending. JET may approve and activate, return for correction, block, request evidence or cancel. No public production route exists until JET activates the first release.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Post-launch publication
Decision_Register.decision: After initial activation, roots may publish ordinary low-risk releases when self-publication controls pass. JET approval remains required for domain activation, ownership change, controlled legal content, JET review blocks, restoration after JET suspension and other specifically governed high-risk changes. JET is not required for every logo, color, copy or permitted availability update.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Scheduled-publication failure
Decision_Register.decision: A scheduled release is published only if every required readiness condition still passes at the effective time. If blocked, the current active release remains, root and JET are notified, the draft remains correctable or reschedulable and public users never see a partial release.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Reverting to an earlier valid presentation
Decision_Register.decision: A root may create a new draft from a prior valid release. JET may immediately restore a prior valid presentation for legal, security or severe operations. Revert creates a new release, preserves replaced history, does not alter past transactions or communications and revalidates current product, route and participant readiness.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Custom-domain request flow
Decision_Register.decision: Custom-domain request follows a fixed flow: proposed domain, ownership confirmation, required external steps, verification, preview, continuity review, activation submission and JET activation. Roots never configure certificates, platform routing, infrastructure secrets or DNS automation directly.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Domain status experience
Decision_Register.decision: Domain lifecycle is REQUESTED, ACTION_REQUIRED, VERIFIED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED and RETIRED. Administration shows current state, root and JET actions, verification, primary domain, previous route and redirect, last check and user-safe failure. Only one domain is active as primary public production route.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Referral-link management experience
Decision_Register.decision: Referral-link management shows participant, type, responsible organization, assigned agent, channel, optional product entry, status, creation and last use, basic entry count, copy, revoke, replace and readiness. Downlines see only their organization and affiliated-agent links. Campaign building, vanity URL and custom tracking-rule configuration are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Participant-management experience
Decision_Register.decision: Participant management shows M05 organization and relationship status, marketplace participation, channels, link status, support, readiness, blockers, dates and allowed actions. Root may enable, suspend or end participation without changing M05 lifecycle. Custom routing formulas and participant-specific product catalogues are excluded.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace operational-health view
Decision_Register.decision: Root and JET administrators see operational health for lifecycle, release, domain, assets, bilingual content, product and carrier availability, participants, referral links, support, integrations, routing exceptions, propagation and M00, M05 and M01 compatibility gates. Each blocker identifies its canonical owner and is never presented as an editable M04 value when owned elsewhere.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Fixed marketplace exceptions
Decision_Register.decision: M04 uses the M00 task and exception framework with fixed types for missing assets, incomplete English or Spanish, inaccessible colors, invalid domain, missing support or disclosure, no entitled channel, no ready product, no eligible participant, invalid link, unavailable participant, routing conflict, blocked schedule, propagation failure, unapproved prior-module delta, suspension review and ending review. Agencies cannot create types.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Exception ownership and escalation
Decision_Register.decision: The root owns ordinary brand, general copy, bilingual completion, support, channel, product-presentation, participant, referral, scheduling and root-suspension issues. Canonical source modules own organization, product, affiliation, licensing, document and integration blockers. JET owns domain activation, security and legal blocks, routing infrastructure, initial activation, emergencies, owner transition, cross-tenant conflict, prior-module activation governance and platform correction. Escalation uses M00 work.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace change notifications
Decision_Register.decision: M04 produces controlled English and Spanish notifications for draft creation, activation submission and outcome, activation, suspension and reactivation, ending schedule, brand publication, blocked schedule, domain action, domain activation or suspension, product-path disablement, participant enablement or block, referral revocation or replacement, propagation failure and JET override or restoration. M10 later owns final templates and delivery.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace history
Decision_Register.decision: Root and JET administrators review immutable history for creation, lifecycle, brand and content versions, availability, participant and routing, support, domain, publication, links, root actions, JET override, readiness and propagation. History records actual actor, acting organization, before and after, effective date, reason, release, correlation and time. Downlines see only their participation and links.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Public marketplace entry resolution
Decision_Register.decision: Public entry may arrive through the active primary domain, approved JET-managed route, valid agency or agent referral or another approved link. Before personal data, M04 resolves and displays marketplace, brand, language, owner, entry attribution, pathways and support. Unknown or invalid routes fail closed with no cross-marketplace or cross-tenant fallback.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace home and journey start
Decision_Register.decision: The public home shows only enabled pathways and does not create a canonical journey merely from a page view. A journey starts after the user selects an enabled path, confirms marketplace or referral context where required and begins the first governed shopping or employer step. M04 supplies release, language, channel, attribution and support to the owning module.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Deep-link entry
Decision_Register.decision: A deep link opens a fixed pathway entry only after M04 validates marketplace, route, channel, product, participant or referral, language and readiness. If unavailable, a marketplace-branded state offers only approved explicit alternatives and never silently changes channel, product, marketplace, responsible organization or journey.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Returning users and existing records
Decision_Register.decision: A returning user signing in through a marketplace sees only records available in that marketplace and authorized context. A secure record link may return to the original marketplace after identification. Another marketplace does not expose, merge or transfer records. A new referral may offer explicit resume-original, start-new or governed transfer or assistance choice.

Decision_Register.topic: Administration, Preview, Consumer Entry and Operational Flows
Decision_Register.title: Marketplace operational insights
Decision_Register.decision: The administration home shows current operational counts for visits, pathway starts, referral entries, consumer, agent and employer starts, no-ready-product results, assistance requests, routing exceptions, publication failures and domain failures without sensitive consumer data. M24 owns historical trends, conversion, attribution analysis and configurable reporting.

Forward_Contract_Register.candidate_contract: Consume MarketplaceContext, enabled state, product line, carrier and release references when publishing product readiness.
Provide product, carrier, service-area, effective-date and readiness summaries to M04.
Publish a governed block that immediately removes new marketplace presentation.
Consume marketplace, release, availability, organization, language and support context.
Consume the same marketplace entry contract when downstream products are ready.
Retain original MarketplaceRelease and responsible organization history.
Provide active agency profile and administrator readiness for M05 organizations.
Provide affiliation, status and agency context for a requested marketplace route.
Display M04-owned link status without owning or regenerating the token.
Consume M05 and M04 effective participant scope.
Return organization and agent authority by product, carrier, state and channel.
Publish events that suspend M04 agent routing and links.
Create leads with entry source, responsible organization, agent and release context.
Consume M04 responsible-organization queue and reassignment reason.
Preserve explicit consent when responsibility or assistance changes.
Consume brand, content language, owner, responsibility, agent, support and release versions.
Provide approved English and Spanish templates for M04 operational events.
Send M04-generated links without modifying token or marketplace association.
Store and scan M04 fixed assets with M04 purpose and version references.
Apply MarketplaceRelease and brand version to generated output where approved.
Preserve original marketplace and current support without bypassing document controls.
Consume EMPLOYER channel, organization, agent, language, geography and release context.
Ignore later referral attribution for an existing employer quote unless governed transfer occurs.
Provide standalone, add-on or bundled product behavior and readiness to M04.
Consume M04 state, carrier and channel presentation without allowing M04 to define product semantics.
Persist MarketplaceContext and MarketplaceRelease versions as analytics dimensions.
Persist fixed entry source, participant, routing and reassignment history without changing operational routing.
Provide historical trends beyond M04 current operational counts.
Retain marketplace, release, responsible organization, agent, channel and product references.
Reject ordinary marketplace reassignment after submission or signature.
Provide current support while preserving historical marketplace evidence.
Consume only approved M04/M01 deltas for marketplace route, brand, language, attribution and release.
Consume approved marketplace and responsible-agency context without making M04 the recommendation owner.
Preserve marketplace, organization and release references through handoff.
Add M04 MarketplaceContext and release version only through approved M00 delta.
Allow M00 workspaces and authentication presentation to consume M04 brand reference.
Enforce fail-closed route resolution and non-authorizing referral context.
Expose M04 participant, support and release references in M05 read models only after approved delta.
Allow M04 to reevaluate participants and revoke routing on M05 changes.
Preserve stable owner, route and release contracts without implementing multiple marketplaces.
Preserve routing reason and assignment history without implementing weighted, skills or AI routing.
